extracted.intended_audience: short story authors and anthology editors (submissions/selection for The Best American Short Stories)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and procedural rules used to determine which previously published American/Canadian short stories are eligible and chosen for inclusion in The Best American Short Stories anthology series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original publication in nationally distributed American or Canadian periodicals
rubrics_metrics.description: Original publication in nationally distributed American or Canadian periodicals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories must have been first published in magazines or online publications that are nationally distributed in the United States or Canada; this is an eligibility requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author nationality/home requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Author is American or Canadian (or has made the U.S. their home)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must be American or Canadian citizens or have made the United States their home in order to be eligible for inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original publication as short stories (no novel excerpts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Original publication as short stories — novel excerpts not considered
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works must have been originally published as short stories; excerpts from longer works such as novels are explicitly ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previously published only (no unpublished work)
rubrics_metrics.description: Must be previously published (no unpublished work)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only stories that have already appeared in eligible periodicals are considered; unpublished manuscripts are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Series Editor selection of 'Notable Stories' (~120)
rubrics_metrics.description: Series Editor selects ~120 notable stories from hundreds of magazines and online publications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The series editor (historically Heidi Pitlor since 2007) reviews a wide range of publications and compiles a list of roughly 120 'Notable Stories' which functions as the first-stage filter for consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guest Editor final selection (~20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guest Editor selects ~20 final stories for the volume
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A guest editor (a leading writer who changes annually) chooses approximately 20 stories from the series editor's notable list to appear in the published volume; this is the final selection stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notable Stories list as a quality bar
rubrics_metrics.description: The series editor's 'Notable Stories' list is itself a quality bar
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being included on the 'Notable Stories' list signals a baseline of quality; authors/items on this list have effectively passed an initial editorial quality threshold even if not chosen for the final volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guest editor's idiosyncratic vision
rubrics_metrics.description: Guest editor's idiosyncratic vision shapes each year's volume
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final selections reflect the personal tastes and aesthetic priorities of the guest editor for that year, so choices may vary in predictable or idiosyncratic ways across volumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Range across styles and genre boundaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Range across literary realism, experimental, genre-adjacent literary work
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The series aims to represent a spectrum of contemporary short fiction, including literary realism, experimental pieces, and work that sits near or within genre traditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for character-driven, language-attentive, emotionally resonant work
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selected stories often emphasize strong character development, careful/attentive use of language, and emotional resonance; these are recurring qualities observed in chosen pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical judgment over popularity
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Best' framing connotes critical, not just popular, judgment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selections are made with an emphasis on critical assessment and literary merit rather than purely on popular success or sales figures.
